rv.q: A lunatic farce that's as black as a policeman's hat, 'The Ladykillers' is as irresistible as ever.
With a little extra pace, this highly entertaining revival will match the original.

The comic high point remains the appearance of a gaggle of over-excited old ladies who turn up to hear the gangsters give a Boccherini recital. The new cast are a generally accomplished gang, each mining new laughs in often unexpected areas.
This approach deprives the tale of all its subtlety and shadowy strangeness.
It is a slightly chaotic but overall enjoyable performance with some laugh out loud moments.

cn.t: An anarchic, slapstick-heavy adaptation that divides critics. While most praise the excellent comic timing and fast-paced physical comedy, some find it lacks the nuance of the original Ealing film.
